# Human adoption of LLM vocabulary in speech and writing — facts

## How it works

- [statement] A preregistered experiment (496 participants) found brief chatbot interaction makes participants adopt specific words, persisting through distractor tasks, supporting exposure-to-active-vocabulary as the mechanism. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01754 · keywords: Human adoption of LLM vocabulary in speech and writing

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Florida State University (Juzek et al.) analysed 22.1 million words of science/tech conversational podcasts; nearly three-quarters of target AI buzzwords rose after ChatGPT, some more than doubling. 'Underscore' rose while its synonym 'accentuate' did not, which points to AI-specific rather than generic drift. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-08-26) — https://news.fsu.edu/news/education-society/2025/08/26/on-screen-and-now-irl-fsu-researchers-find-evidence-suggesting-chatgpt-influences-how-we-speak/ · keywords: Human adoption of LLM vocabulary in speech and writing · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01754

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Yakura et al. (Max Planck) analysed about 737,083 hours of unscripted conversation from 824,634 podcast episodes and report that ChatGPT-favoured words (delve, showcase, boast, meticulous) rose abruptly in spontaneous speech after ChatGPT's release; they use synthetic-control analysis to argue for a causal link. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-16) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01754 · keywords: Human adoption of LLM vocabulary in speech and writing · also: https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/chatgpt-is-changing-the-words-we-use-in-conversation/
- [statement] The 'GPT words' list was derived by having ChatGPT edit millions of emails, essays and articles and extracting words it repeatedly added; usage was then tracked in about 360,000 YouTube academic talks and 771,000 podcast episodes, with a surge within roughly 18 months of release. (medium confidence) — https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/chatgpt-is-changing-the-words-we-use-in-conversation/ · keywords: Human adoption of LLM vocabulary in speech and writing · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01754
- [statement] The measured effect is lexical only; the Max Planck paper does not test semantic or grammatical influence and frames vocabulary as an early indicator of wider cultural influence. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01754 · keywords: Human adoption of LLM vocabulary in speech and writing · also: https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/chatgpt-is-changing-the-words-we-use-in-conversation/
